title: The Turán number of Berge paths in connected hypergraphs
summary: A Berge path in a hypergraph is an alternating sequence of distinct vertices and edges $v_1,e_1, v_2, \ldots, e_{k-1}, v_{k}$ such that $v_i, v_{i+1} \in e_i$ for all $i \in [k-1]$. Győri, Katona, and Lemons determined the maximum number edges in $r$-uniform, $n$-vertex hypergraphs without Berge paths on $k$ vertices. The extremal examples for their bounds are disconnected hypergraphs in which each component has either too few edges or too few vertices to contain such a Berge path.
